 There’s an event coming up on Saturday, Nov. 14 that suits all the multitaskers out there. The Alcoa High School Holiday Market is the opportunity to shop for Christmas gifts, help local students, learn about a worthy cause and support small businesses — all on that one day.
 It’s the 10th annual Holiday Market set from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m on Nov. 14. DECA and marketing students take the lead every year, under the guidance of teachers Joy Gornto and Keenan Sudderth. This year’s no different, except there’s the added pressure of making the 10th show extra special.
 “The three girls that did it last year are now seniors,” Gornto said. “They are involved in a lot of things. The thought was to get some younger students to get invovlved. Then these three showed up asking to learn.”
 Presley Harmon, Aliyah Hill and Shani Love — they are the ones who took on the challenge. All three are sophomores, involved in DECA and are also cheerleaders at AHS. They took on this task that challenges their own multitasking talents.
 As Gornto pointed out, there will be 75 vendors selling everything from soaps to stained glass, ornaments, wreaths, hand-painted items, food products, cards, toys, jewelry, hats, scarves and lots more. That first year, 32 vendors signed on; this annual event now has a waiting list.
 The three sophomores not only are organizing this huge project, but also a new component this year. A scholarship will be awarded to a marketing student at AHS in honor or Garrison Stephens, a former marketing student diagnosed with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) while he was a senior. Love has designed a t-shirt and the football team will be wearing special emblems on their helmets on Friday night. Cheerleaders and others are selling t-shirts, with proceeds going toward the scholarship. Those who applied for the Garrison Stephens Marketing Scholarship had to do research on ALS and write about what they learned.
 Gornto and a committee has narrowed down the list of possible scholarship winners to four. Stephens and his family will make the final decision at the Friday football game.
 A kids area is also being added to this year’s market, said these organizers. Presley, Hill and Love are relying on help from classmates, including Student Council to pitch in for the day-long event. Hill said jobs between her and the other lead organizers have been split evenly. “There are a bunch of moving parts,” she said.
 Setup and takedown are all part of the staging; being onsite at 7 a.m. on Nov. 14 to get things rolling isn’t a favorite of these teens, but they won’t complain. Gornto said the vendors love this show because the students help them carry supplies inside and stay throughout the day. “It’s a huge help,” she said. “They say our event is one of their favorites.”
 Teamwork, organizational skills, management training and communications — Love, Hill and Presley said they have learned it all through this process. All three of them expressed interest in running their own businesses some day.
 “This is a mini business,” Gornto told them. After 14 years at AHS, Gornto is retiring to start her own business. “After teaching entrepreneurship to them all this time, I am going to do that.”
 Culinary students at AHS are also participating in this event on Saturday with their own food truck.
 As the organizers know, there is one more component to add. Getting the word out is key to getting people to attend. Each year, about 1,200 people come see what it’s all about and take home gifts for themselves or others. Television interviews, advertising on social media and word of mouth are what these marketing students know best. This market now has a strong following, Gornto said.
 “People like to see that students are putting it together,” this teacher said. “They like to support education. And they like to shop. This year, they are supporting a good cause. This is doing everything at once by showing up.”

 Alcoa High School Holiday Market
 Alcoa High School Holiday Market
 When: From 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 14
 Where: Alcoa High School, 1205 Lodge St., Alcoa
 Who: There will be 75 vendors selling everything from holiday cards and decor to food items, stained glass, clothing and more. Food trucks will also be on hand.
 Admission: Free
 Proceeds: Going to DECA program and to fund a scholarship for a marketing student.
